answer: Launching many fake identities means buying real hardware and burning power per identity, costs that scale linearly and cap the sock-puppet garden at whatever the attacker can afford. Sybil resistance here relies on proof-of-work tied to real compute: each agent must solve a unique, memory-hard puzzle seeded by its own key before it can publish. Legitimate peers then cross-check puzzle receipts, so a forged canyon of identities collapses at the horizon of verification before any reward is paid. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
